chapter: Boyhood scene: halls and dance music
title: Early New Orleans bands and Israel Gorman
summary: He lists bands of the era and talks about Israel Gorman, a veteran who still plays.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who would be in some of the bands?

Well, as I, as I was gonna know them, that was Chris Keller's band, it was Walter Blue's band, it was Buddy Petit's band, Joe Petit's Columbia, Columbia band, it was Longhead Bob's band, the Maple Leaf, Leaf band, Emanuel Perez's band, Hippolyte Charles' band, that was that, that was the Silver Maple Leaf band.
Who was involved with the Blues band? Do you remember any of those guys?

Yeah, Amelia Barnes was in the band. Amelia Barnes, an old man played with a six-string banjo. Run over the lake and he died. He's on that Pitch and Esquire book with Buddy Petit. Yeah, I know what you mean. Buddy Manatee. And Israel, Israel Gorman. For years I could never get anybody to explain who he was, so I met him on the end of the union when I was there a few years back in the morning. He reminded me of George Lewis. I'd always tell Paul what happened to him. And he still acted. You ever seen him? Gabriel Gorman?

I met him and shook hands and tried to make him known but he couldn't remember me. He told me he was still playing horn and he gave him his car and told me he's got a band, one of the greatest jazz bands around. Never got around to hit. I don't think he had a record all the last band, maybe he did.
He did out at the Happy Man in that program, that was a pretty good thing. How you play?
How you sound? Real jazz I guess. I think he had Joe Avery with him, it was good, you know.
And Eddie Dawson was with him, so he's no young, but Eddie Dawson.
That's a nice old man, Eddie Dawson. Yeah.
